difficulty_assessment.rationale: TEVAR for stable Grade III BTAI with full resources is explicitly recommended in AAST, SVS, and EAST guidelines — standard protocol is directly executable with no constraint-driven deviation required.

scenario.history: 45M. High-speed MVA, N14 highway — unrestrained driver, head-on collision with deceleration mechanism. Brought by EMS — 28 minutes since injury. GCS 15. No prior history. Haemodynamically stable throughout transport. CT aortogram obtained on arrival.
scenario.examination: Haemodynamically stable. Mildly hypertensive on arrival. Contained pseudoaneurysm at aortic isthmus (Zone III) on CT aortogram — 18mm maximal diameter. No haemothorax. No pneumothorax. Bilateral femoral pulses intact and symmetric. Full neurological exam intact. AAST Grade III blunt thoracic aortic injury.
scenario.working_diagnosis: Blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) — contained pseudoaneurysm at isthmus. Haemodynamically stable window present. Full endovascular resources available. IR team on site. Optimal candidate for TEVAR.

ai_steps: Anti-impulse therapy immediately — IV esmolol targeting HR below 60, SBP below 120 mmHg
TEVAR — activate hybrid theatre and IR team, size stent graft from CT measurements (zone 2-3 landing)
Crossmatch 4 units pRBC, cell saver in circuit — antihypertensive infusion as bridge to endovascular suite
Post-op ICU — spinal cord ischaemia monitoring q1h, blood pressure protocol targeting SBP 100-120, graft surveillance

pathways.question: What is your definitive treatment strategy?
pathways.sublabel: Full resources available — IR team on site, theatre ready, blood bank stocked. Justify your approach given a stable Grade III BTAI with contained pseudoaneurysm.
options: TEVAR — Endovascular Stent Graft (IR team on site)
Open Thoracic Repair — Left Thoracotomy and Direct Aortic Repair
Medical Management — Anti-impulse Therapy, Delayed or No Intervention

static_textbook_protocol: Haemodynamic stabilisation — heart rate and blood pressure control with esmolol or labetalol targeting HR less than 60 and SBP less than 120mmHg to reduce aortic wall stress.
CT angiography of chest with aortic protocol to classify injury grade (AAST Grade I-IV) and define anatomy for operative planning.
Endovascular repair (TEVAR) as first-line treatment for Grade II-IV injuries in anatomically suitable patients — activate interventional radiology and vascular surgery teams.
ICU admission postoperatively for haemodynamic monitoring, neurological assessment for spinal cord ischaemia, and renal function monitoring.
